description: This topic explains how the human eye, lens camera, simple and compound microscopes, astronomical telescope and projector use lenses to form images, including vision defects, magnification and the uses of each instrument.

mcq.questionText: Which part of the human eye does most of the bending (refraction) of light entering the eye?
mcq.explanation: The curved cornea is where light first enters and is refracted most. The eye lens only makes fine adjustments to bring the image to a sharp focus on the retina.

mcq.questionText: The light-sensitive screen at the back of the eye on which images are formed is the:
mcq.explanation: The retina contains light-sensitive cells that detect the image and send signals to the brain through the optic nerve.

mcq.questionText: The part of the eye that controls the amount of light entering by changing the size of the pupil is the:
mcq.explanation: The iris is the coloured part of the eye. It adjusts the size of the pupil to let in more light in dim conditions and less light in bright conditions.

mcq.questionText: The ability of the eye lens to change its focal length so that objects at different distances can be focused clearly is called:
mcq.explanation: Accommodation is the adjustment of the curvature (and therefore focal length) of the eye lens by the ciliary muscles to focus objects at different distances.

mcq.questionText: The image formed on the retina of a normal eye is:
mcq.explanation: Like a converging lens forming an image of a distant object, the eye forms a real, inverted and diminished image on the retina. The brain interprets it as upright.

mcq.questionText: A short-sighted (myopic) person can see near objects clearly but distant objects appear blurred. This defect is corrected using a:
mcq.explanation: In short sight the image of a distant object forms in front of the retina. A concave (diverging) lens spreads the rays so the image falls on the retina.

mcq.questionText: Long sight (hypermetropia) is corrected by wearing spectacles fitted with a:
mcq.explanation: In long sight the image of a near object forms behind the retina. A convex (converging) lens brings the rays together sooner so the image forms on the retina.

mcq.questionText: Which part of a lens camera plays the same role as the iris of the eye?
mcq.explanation: The diaphragm controls the size of the aperture, regulating how much light enters the camera, just as the iris controls the pupil in the eye.

mcq.questionText: In a lens camera, focusing on objects at different distances is done by:

options.text: Changing the shape of the lens
Moving the lens nearer to or farther from the film
Changing the size of the aperture

mcq.explanation: Unlike the eye, the camera lens has a fixed focal length, so focusing is achieved by moving the lens to change the lens-to-film distance.

mcq.questionText: A simple microscope (magnifying glass) is simply a:

options.text: Single convex lens of short focal length

mcq.explanation: A magnifying glass is a single converging (convex) lens of short focal length used to view a magnified, upright, virtual image of a near object.

mcq.questionText: To produce a magnified virtual image with a simple microscope, the object must be placed:

options.text: Between the lens and its principal focus (within F)

mcq.explanation: When the object is placed between the lens and its focal point, a convex lens forms a magnified, upright, virtual image on the same side as the object.

mcq.questionText: A compound microscope uses two convex lenses called the:
mcq.explanation: A compound microscope has an objective lens (short focal length) near the object and an eyepiece lens through which the final magnified image is viewed.

mcq.questionText: In a normal-adjustment astronomical telescope, the objective lens used has a:
mcq.explanation: An astronomical telescope uses an objective of long focal length and an eyepiece of short focal length to give high angular magnification of distant objects.

mcq.questionText: The final image seen through an astronomical telescope in normal adjustment is:
mcq.explanation: The astronomical telescope produces a magnified, virtual, inverted image. The inversion does not matter when viewing stars and planets.

mcq.questionText: A projector is used to throw a large image of a slide or film onto a screen. The image it forms is:
mcq.explanation: A projector uses a converging lens with the slide placed between F and 2F to form a real, inverted, magnified image on the screen. The slide is placed upside down so the picture appears upright.

fib.questionText: The coloured part of the eye that controls the size of the pupil is called the _____.
fib.explanation: The iris is the coloured ring of muscle that opens or narrows the pupil to control the amount of light entering the eye.

fib.questionText: The hole in the middle of the iris through which light passes into the eye is the _____.
fib.explanation: The pupil is the opening that lets light reach the lens and retina; its size is adjusted by the iris.

fib.questionText: The adjustment of the focal length of the eye lens to focus objects at different distances is called _____.
fib.explanation: Ciliary muscles change the curvature of the eye lens during accommodation, altering its focal length.

fib.questionText: Short sight (myopia) is corrected by using a _____ lens.
fib.explanation: A concave (diverging) lens diverges light so that the image of a distant object falls on the retina instead of in front of it.

fib.questionText: Long sight (hypermetropia) is corrected by using a _____ lens.
fib.explanation: A convex (converging) lens converges light so the image of a near object forms on the retina instead of behind it.

fib.questionText: In a lens camera, the part that opens and closes quickly to control the time light enters is the _____.
fib.explanation: The shutter controls the exposure time, while the diaphragm controls the amount of light.

fib.questionText: A magnifying glass is also known as a _____ microscope.
fib.explanation: A simple microscope is a single convex lens of short focal length used to magnify small near objects.

fib.questionText: In a compound microscope, the lens close to the object being viewed is called the _____ lens.
fib.explanation: The objective lens forms a real, magnified image which is then further magnified by the eyepiece.

fib.questionText: The number of times an instrument increases the apparent size of an object is called the _____.
fib.explanation: Magnification is the ratio of the image size to the object size (or image distance to object distance for a lens).

fib.questionText: The light-sensitive layer at the back of the eye on which the image is formed is the _____.
fib.explanation: The retina detects the image and sends nerve signals to the brain through the optic nerve.

tf.questionText: The cornea does most of the refraction of light entering the eye.
tf.explanation: The cornea provides most of the eye's converging power; the eye lens makes only the fine adjustments needed for sharp focus.

tf.questionText: The image formed on the retina of a normal eye is upright and magnified.
tf.explanation: The retinal image is real, inverted and diminished. The brain interprets it as upright.

tf.questionText: In short sight, the image of a distant object is formed in front of the retina.
tf.explanation: A short-sighted eye is too powerful or too long, so distant objects focus in front of the retina, making them blurred.

tf.questionText: Long sight is corrected by using a concave (diverging) lens.
tf.explanation: Long sight is corrected with a convex (converging) lens; concave lenses are used for short sight.

tf.questionText: A camera lens focuses on different objects by changing the curvature of the lens, just like the eye.
tf.explanation: A camera lens has a fixed focal length and focuses by moving the lens toward or away from the film, unlike the eye which changes its lens shape.

tf.questionText: A simple microscope forms a virtual, upright and magnified image.
tf.explanation: With the object placed within the focal length, a convex lens gives a virtual, upright, magnified image on the same side as the object.

tf.questionText: In a compound microscope the eyepiece has a longer focal length than the objective.
tf.explanation: In a compound microscope both lenses have short focal lengths, and the objective has the shorter focal length to give high magnification.

tf.questionText: An astronomical telescope is used to view distant objects such as stars and planets.
tf.explanation: The astronomical telescope magnifies the angular size of very distant objects, making them appear larger and clearer.

tf.questionText: A projector forms a real, magnified image on a screen.
tf.explanation: With the slide placed between F and 2F of the converging lens, the projector forms a real, inverted, magnified image on the screen.

tf.questionText: The diaphragm in a camera and the iris in the eye perform similar functions.
tf.explanation: Both control the amount of light entering: the iris adjusts the pupil and the diaphragm adjusts the camera aperture.

summary.questionText: Name the main parts of the human eye involved in forming an image.
summary.correctAnswer: Cornea, pupil, iris, lens and retina.
summary.explanation: Light passes through the cornea and pupil, is focused by the lens, and forms an image on the retina; the iris controls the light entering.

summary.questionText: What is accommodation of the eye?
summary.correctAnswer: The changing of the eye lens shape (and focal length) by the ciliary muscles to focus objects at different distances.
summary.explanation: Accommodation lets us see both near and distant objects clearly by adjusting the lens curvature.

summary.questionText: State the cause and correction of short sight (myopia).
summary.correctAnswer: Cause: the image of distant objects forms in front of the retina; corrected using a concave (diverging) lens.
summary.explanation: The eyeball is too long or the lens too strong, so a diverging lens is needed to move the image back onto the retina.

summary.questionText: State the cause and correction of long sight (hypermetropia).
summary.correctAnswer: Cause: the image of near objects forms behind the retina; corrected using a convex (converging) lens.
summary.explanation: The eyeball is too short or the lens too weak, so a converging lens helps form the image on the retina.

summary.questionText: Give two similarities between the eye and the lens camera.
summary.correctAnswer: Both use a convex lens to form a real, inverted, diminished image on a screen, and both control the amount of light entering (iris/diaphragm).
summary.explanation: The retina acts like the film/sensor, and both have a light-controlling aperture.

summary.questionText: State one key difference between how the eye and the camera focus.
summary.correctAnswer: The eye focuses by changing the shape of its lens, while the camera focuses by moving the lens toward or away from the film.
summary.explanation: The eye lens has a variable focal length; the camera lens has a fixed focal length.

summary.questionText: Describe the image produced by a simple microscope (magnifying glass).
summary.correctAnswer: A virtual, upright and magnified image, formed when the object is placed within the focal length of the convex lens.
summary.explanation: This is why a magnifying glass is used to read small print or examine small objects.

summary.questionText: Name the two lenses of a compound microscope and state their use.
summary.correctAnswer: The objective lens (near the object) forms a real magnified image, and the eyepiece lens magnifies it further to give a large virtual image.
summary.explanation: Two-stage magnification allows very high overall magnification for tiny objects like cells.

summary.questionText: State two uses of an astronomical telescope and a projector.
summary.correctAnswer: A telescope is used to view distant objects such as stars and planets; a projector is used to display a large image of a slide or film on a screen.
summary.explanation: Each instrument applies lenses for a specific purpose: magnifying distant objects or enlarging images for an audience.

summary.questionText: Define magnification of an optical instrument.
summary.correctAnswer: Magnification is the ratio of the size of the image to the size of the object (m = image size / object size).
summary.explanation: It tells how many times larger the image appears compared with the actual object.

hoq.questionText: A student in Dodoma can read a book clearly but cannot read the chalkboard from the back of the class. An optician should prescribe spectacles with which type of lens, and why?

options.text: Convex lenses, to converge light onto the retina
Concave lenses, because the image of distant objects forms in front of the retina
Plane glass, because the eye is normal
Concave mirrors, to reflect light into the eye

hoq.explanation: The student is short-sighted (myopic): near objects are clear but distant ones blurred because their image forms in front of the retina. A concave (diverging) lens corrects this by moving the image back onto the retina.

hoq.questionText: A teacher wants to project a slide so that the picture appears large and the right way up on a screen. Where should the slide be placed relative to the lens, and how should it be oriented?

options.text: Within the focal length F and placed upright
Between F and 2F and placed upside down
At the focal point F and placed upright

hoq.explanation: A projector forms a real, inverted, magnified image when the object is between F and 2F. Because the image is inverted, the slide is placed upside down so the picture appears upright on the screen.

hoq.questionText: A laboratory technician needs to examine very tiny cells that a single magnifying glass cannot enlarge enough. Which instrument and arrangement should be used to obtain the highest magnification?

options.text: An astronomical telescope with a long-focus objective
A compound microscope with a short-focus objective and a short-focus eyepiece
A lens camera with a wide aperture
A projector with the slide beyond 2F

hoq.explanation: A compound microscope magnifies in two stages: the short-focus objective forms a real magnified image which the short-focus eyepiece magnifies again, giving much higher magnification than a single lens for viewing tiny objects such as cells.
